A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiTAR research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated results.

before.justification: v1 reports original DiTAR speech-generation results, subjective evaluations, scaling experiments, ablations and inference analyses, including Seed benchmark and temperature results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally reports latency and real-time-factor measurements in Table 7.

M1.justification: The architecture, training objectives and conditioning remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 locally revises temperature sampling: argmax becomes argmin for selecting the injection index, and reinjection coefficients change from t_n to t_{n+1}. These are revisions to the written inference procedure; the PDFs do not establish changes to its implementation.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage remains LibriLight, Emilia, LibriSpeech subsets A/B, Seed-EN and Seed-ZH, with the same scaling and inference scenarios. Seed-ZH was already evaluated in v1 Appendix B.1 despite its table incorrectly repeating the Seed-EN heading.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the LibriSpeech, subjective, Seed and efficiency comparisons. v3 Table 3 retains every comparator from v1 Table 6. The new MAR/Fluid/ARDiT diagram is conceptual rather than an evaluated baseline comparison.

E3.justification: Section 4.5.2 adds first-frame latency, explicitly excluding the vocoder, and real-time factor at batch sizes 1 and 500. These supplement the existing throughput protocol using matched parameter sizes, an A100, 10-second outputs and CFG with NFE=10. Existing speech-evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 7 extends the efficiency analysis by examining first-frame latency versus total generation speed for NAR and DiTAR patch sizes 2/4 across two batch sizes. Existing scaling, patch-size, historical-context, guidance and temperature analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point-estimate reporting without added seed information, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The subjective evaluation and 500-sample diversity analysis retain their reporting practices.

E6.justification: v3 Table 7 adds runtime results: at batch size 1, DiTAR(P=4) reports 0.066-second latency and 0.66 RTF, versus NAR's 0.37 seconds and 0.037. All seven matched tables retain their numerical values; the Seed and temperature tables are relocated results.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the formal injection-index selection from maximizing to minimizing the distance between the discretized time and temperature. This is a local mathematical correction. The probability factorization, diffusion equations, predicted-data derivation and computational-cost derivations otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about patch-based LM–diffusion modeling, temperature sampling, scalability and state-of-the-art zero-shot speech generation with reduced computation.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly interprets the latency/RTF tradeoff: autoregression enables earlier output, while NAR benefits from parallelism at small batches, and patch size adjusts this balance. LM guidance is newly explained through its computational savings. The fairness statement also stops claiming that training sets are standardized.

D1.justification: v3 identifies the model behind the retained Seed results as having 1B parameters trained on 280k hours, and specifies 280k hours for component scaling. These are additional disclosures, not established experiment changes. It also adds a project-page pointer; existing hardware, optimizer and architecture details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to classifier-free guidance for language models and LLaVA-NeXT-Interleave. Section 3.3 shifts the guidance comparison toward computational efficiency, while new Appendix C and Figure 9 explicitly contrast DiTAR with MAR/Fluid and ARDiT. The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained, with localized rewriting of guidance and efficiency explanations, section renaming and movement of appendix material into the main narrative. v3 also duplicates the Scaling Behaviors discussion in Sections 4.2 and 4.3, disrupting the experimental section's organization.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the two-column conference layout with a single-column report design and extensively resizes and relocates displays. It moves Algorithm 1 and appendix tables into the main text and adds Table 7 and Figure 9. Figure 4's guidance ticks change from 1–4 to 0–3, and the Seed-ZH table heading is corrected.

improvement.justification: Table 7 usefully extends v1's throughput analysis by exposing latency versus total-generation-speed tradeoffs. Additional model-setting disclosures and corrections to guidance labels and injection-index selection improve clarity. These are limited gains because the benchmark evidence is unchanged, and duplicated scaling prose and remaining pseudocode inconsistencies constrain the improvement.
